itens.descricao: Ibovespa sobe e dólar recua com mercado atento a pesquisas e reta final das eleições Exame
trechos: B3: pesquisas eleitorais e recuperação de Wall Street movem o pregão.
Publicado em 19 de outubro de 2026 às 11h01.
Última atualização em 19 de outubro de 2026 às 11h04.

O Ibovespa opera em alta nesta segunda-feira, 19, apoiado por bancos, varejistas e ações ligadas à economia doméstica, enquanto investidores acompanham a reta final da eleição presidencial e a recuperação das ações de tecnologia em Nova York.
Por volta das 11h (horário de Brasília), o principal índice da B3 avançava 0,68%, aos 206.818 pontos.
O dólar comercial recua 0,53%, cotado a R$ 5,047.
A Vale (VALE3) contribui para o índice, com alta de 1,24%.
Petrobras, por outro lado, limita o avanço: PETR4 cai 1,46% e PETR3 recua 1,19%.

itens.titulo: Lumentum (LITE) Can’t Meet Demand. Can Its Valuation Hold Up?
itens.descricao: Lumentum (LITE) Can’t Meet Demand. Can Its Valuation Hold Up? Yahoo Finance
trechos: According to Lumentum Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:LITE) CEO Michael Hurlston, the company is now almost sold out of components for 2029, as he said in a recent interview.
Just six months ago, he said Lumentum was on track to sell out by 2028.
Meanwhile, see our Top 10 Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) Stocks to Buy in 2026 to see the 5 companies that rank higher than LITE.
Lumentum cannot meet about 70% of demand for certain products through next year.
For some other products, supply constraints will leave 30% of demand unmet through 2028.
Lumentum's forward P/E stands at 45.70x, roughly 22% above its five-year average of 37.51x.
EPS is projected to grow 151.24% this fiscal year from a small base, followed by another 64.80% increase next year.
Based on current estimates, the P/E could decline to roughly 28x on 2028 earnings and 21x on 2029 earnings.

trechos: By the closing bell on October 16, the S&P 500's technology sector had fallen more than 3%, the Nasdaq had lost about 2%, and energy was the stronger corner of the market with real momentum.

AI and semiconductor stocks were on course to shed more than $1 trillion in combined value during the week as rate-hike fears, worries about AI financing and tougher competition weighed on sentiment, as reported by CNBC.

Also read: Michael Burry pulls an old playbook into the Nvidia fight Jensen Huang's calm meets an AI credit scare Huang also moved to defuse a separate scare around CoreWeave, the debt-heavy cloud provider in which Nvidia holds roughly an 11% stake.
Morgan Stanley estimates AI-related global debt issuance will approach $570 billion in 2026, TheStreet reported.
Reports that OpenAI's annualized revenue was nearing $50 billion, well below figures that had circulated earlier, helped knock Nvidia, Oracle and Micron lower on October 8.
When Nvidia reported results on August 26, he said AI had reached its inflection point, that compute had become revenue and that demand was accelerating.

Consumer prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier in September, with energy costs tied to the Iran conflict doing much of the lifting, and Bank of America was already calling for a Fed rate hike in October.
The 10-year Treasury yield spiked immediately after the report was released on October 14 before calming later in the day.
